History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Adult male with no significant past medical history except eczema and penicillin allergy presented via telemedicine 15 min after a wasp sting, reporting shallow breathing, chest tightness, tingling lips, and blotchy rash; instructed to take oral antihistamine and call an ambulance for possible evolving anaphylaxis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Breathing difficulty after wasp sting.  
• Onset: ~15 minutes prior while gardening.  
• Course: Symptoms developed rapidly after sting; currently shallow breaths, mild chest tightness.  
• Associated symptoms: Tingling of lips (no obvious swelling); blotchy skin rash. No reported throat tightness or wheeze.  
• Aggravating/relieving factors: None tried; has not taken any medication yet.  
• Review of systems: No other symptoms discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Eczema.  
• Aerosinusitis (uses antihistamine prophylactically when flying).  
• No prior episodes of allergic reactions or anaphylaxis.

Medications:
• Antihistamine (name/dose/route/frequency not documented; used intermittently for aerosinusitis).  
Allergies: Penicillin (reaction type not specified).

Social History:
• Lives with wife; wife present and able to assist.  
• Was gardening at home.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use: not discussed.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
(No in-person exam possible via telemedicine)
• Patient verbally reports shallow breathing, chest tightness, tingling lips, blotchy rash.  
• No objective vitals provided.

Investigations:
None performed.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected acute systemic allergic reaction to wasp sting, risk of progression to anaphylaxis.  
• Advise immediate oral antihistamine (available at home).  
• Wife instructed to call emergency medical services (ambulance) rather than self-transport.  
• Emphasized urgency due to potential airway compromise; advised hospital evaluation and monitoring.  
• Educated on signs of worsening (increasing shortness of breath, throat swelling, dizziness).  

General Plan items:  
• Obtain vital signs and consider epinephrine administration en route or on arrival if criteria met (to be done by EMS/hospital).  
• Document reaction and reinforce need for future emergency epinephrine auto-injector prescription once stabilized.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: vitals, full medication list, comprehensive allergy details, smoking/alcohol history.  
• No internal contradictions noted.  
• Transcript quality: clear; occasional minor omissions (patient silence).
